Triggers.value: A specific taste associated with the event

Maladaptive Strategies.value: always sit with back against a wall to see the room
I spend money impulsively to distract or comfort myself

Threat.value: I listen for sounds that might mean someone is entering my home
I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place
I notice potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment

Memory.value: The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me
My memories of the frightening event are like a film that plays over and over.
When I remember the frightening event I feel like it is happening right now.

Negative Appraisals.value: If I think about the event, I will not be able to handle it
I will never be able to feel normal emotions again
Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore

vignette: John, a 73-year-old divorced journalist from North America, experienced a man-made disaster over two decades ago that has left deep psychological scars. The event was so traumatic that it triggered an array of symptoms that have progressively worsened over time. On the day of the disaster, John was at his office when the building suddenly erupted into chaos. The smell of smoke and the taste of ash were overpowering, evoking a sense of complete helplessness. The unpredictability of the situation compounded his terror; he could not anticipate where danger might come from next. Since then, these specific triggers have become almost unbearable for him. John has developed several maladaptive strategies to cope with the constant threat he feels. He now always sits with his back against a wall, ensuring he can see everything around him. This behavior began shortly after the event when even small unpredictable situations triggered intense anxiety. The act of sitting in such a way gave him a false sense of security and control. When he encounters triggers like related photos or tastes reminiscent of the disaster, he freezes completely, unable to respond effectively. The memory of that day is so vivid it feels unreal—like something from a film rather than his own life. John often relives the event in intrusive flashbacks, which are triggered by any unpredictable situation or even certain tastes. These memories replay over and over in his mind, making it nearly impossible for him to relax even when he knows he is safe. The more these memories intrude, the more anxious and threatened he becomes. His fear of the event’s memory and its unpredictability has led John to avoid thinking about it altogether. He believes that if he does think about what happened, he won’t be able to handle it, further reinforcing his compulsive spending as a way to distract himself from these thoughts. This avoidance exacerbates his sense of lost meaning and emotions; everything feels flat and devoid of significance. John’s intrusions are relentless, often triggered by seemingly mundane events at work or in his daily life. The unpredictability of news reporting has become unbearable for him, making it difficult to maintain focus on his job. He listens intently for any sounds that might signal danger, even when he is in a safe environment. This heightened state of alertness makes everyday situations feel threatening. His compulsive spending has spiraled out of control; John buys items impulsively as a way to soothe the anxiety that arises from these memories and triggers. However, this behavior only provides temporary relief and often leaves him feeling more isolated and overwhelmed by guilt for his lack of self-control. The combination of these symptoms has created a vicious cycle. As his intrusive memories persist, they trigger intense emotional responses that fuel his maladaptive strategies and threat perceptions. This reinforces his belief that he cannot handle thinking about the event, leading to further avoidance behaviors. The memory itself becomes both a trigger for anxiety and a result of it. John’s world has narrowed significantly over time. He avoids social gatherings and places where unpredictability might reign supreme. His compulsive spending has put him in financial strain, adding another layer of stress that he cannot seem to escape from. What finally brought John to seek help was a recent incident at work where he froze entirely during an unpredictable situation, unable to act or even speak. He realized then how severely his life had been impacted and how much he feared never feeling normal again. Despite this realization, he is terrified of the prospect of reliving those traumatic memories in therapy but simultaneously hopeful that there might be a way to reclaim some semblance of a normal life.
